column1: # Cross-module fn value in a higher-order word's CLOSURE slot
# A function value resolves its free words in the module that DEFINED it. The
# interpreter now does this at every seam; the compiler cannot yet, because it
# lowers a higher-order word's fn operand to a closure unit compiled against
# the CALLING module. Compiling this body against the caller silently baked the
# caller's `lim` (100) and returned [] where the interpreter returns [3 4] — a
# foreignFnHome therefore DECLINES the lowering, and `filter` islands.
# The island is correct, just slow: the OpFallback span runs the callback seam,
# which routes the body to its defining registry (core.CallBoruFn). The row is
# here rather than in lang/spec/module-fnvalue-boundary.tsv §4 because it is the
# one row of that section the compiler cannot yet model, and the main corpus

import module [def lim fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [2]] def big fn [[e:Map] [Boolean] [(e dot value) gt (lim 0)]] export "A" {big: big/r}] end def lim fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [100]] filter A.big [1 2 3 4]
column3: a cross-module predicate resolves `lim` in its OWN module (2), not the caller's (100)
